# Results — Study 285 (St-Patricks-Day) on ^GSPC daily returns

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). St. Patrick's Day
trading sessions are derived by date arithmetic in [`data.py`](../st_patricks_day/data.py)
(first trading day on/after March 17). ^GSPC daily close-to-close log-returns are
read from the shared repo cache `_cache/^GSPC_split_only.parquet` (price-only, no
dividends). Match the fingerprint below to confirm you hold the same tape.
As-of **2026-06-17**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | n observations | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| ^GSPC daily close (price-only log-return) | 1928-01-03 – 2026-06-12 | 24,728 days | `df3897aef897` |
| St. Patrick sessions | 1928 – 2026 | 99 events | derived (date arithmetic) |

## Primary: St. Patrick session vs baselines

| Comparison | mean / contrast | t-stat | p |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| St. Patrick session (level) | **+14.8 bps** | HAC t = **+1.13** | — |
| vs all other trading days (+2.4 bps) | +12.4 bps | Welch t = +0.93 | 0.353 |
| vs all other March days (+0.7 bps) | +14.1 bps | Welch t = +1.04 | 0.299 |

- The St. Patrick session does average **+14.8 bps**, about six times the +2.4 bps
  unconditional daily drift — but with ~131 bps daily standard deviation across only
  99 events, the **HAC t-stat is just 1.13**, well below the t = 2 inference bar.
- Stripping out generic March seasonality (the "vs other March days" contrast) does
  not help: +14.1 bps richer than the rest of March, Welch **p = 0.299**.

## Placebo: March 24 (one week later)

| metric | value |
|---|--:|
| n events | 99 |
| Mean | +3.5 bps |
| vs other March days, Welch p | 0.877 |

A folklore-free day a week later is essentially flat. There is nothing special
about the late-March neighbourhood; the March-17 number is not echoed by its
neighbours.

## Multiple-comparisons sweep (Bonferroni over 5 March anchor days)

| anchor day | n | mean (bps) | p (raw) | p (Bonferroni ×5) |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 31 | 67 | -24.8 | 0.107 | 0.534 |
| 10 | 99 | +23.1 | 0.265 | 1.000 |
| **17 (St. Patrick)** | 99 | **+14.8** | **0.299** | **1.000** |
| 3 | 99 | +8.6 | 0.433 | 1.000 |
| 24 | 99 | +3.5 | 0.877 | 1.000 |

The most extreme March slot is the 31st (a *negative* −24.8 bps), and even it does
not survive Bonferroni. March 17's raw p of 0.30 becomes ~1.0 once you account for
the five candidate days a snooper could have tested.

## Sub-period split — where the "bump" actually lives

| period | n | mean (bps) | HAC t |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1928–1960 | 33 | **-9.9** | -0.43 |
| 1961–1990 | 30 | **-12.2** | -0.89 |
| 1991–2026 | 36 | **+59.9** | **+3.27** |

This is the kill shot. The entire St. Patrick "bump" is a **1991–2026 phenomenon**
(+59.9 bps, HAC t = 3.27) and is **negative** in both earlier regimes. A genuine
calendar signal does not flip sign across history; an effect that exists only in the
most recent third of the sample is a regime artifact, not a robust edge.

## Could you trade it?

The only implementation is: sit in cash all year, be long the index on the single
St. Patrick session.

- Gross event mean: +14.8 bps (HAC t = 1.13).
- Net of a 2 bps round-trip: **+12.8 bps/event, HAC t = 0.98** — statistically zero.
- Compounded one event per year that is ~+0.13%/yr of exposure for one day, versus
  buy-and-hold capturing the market's drift on all ~250 trading days.

One day of exposure a year cannot compound into a portfolio. There is no vehicle
that beats simply holding the index.

## Positive control

The synthetic generator (`data.synthetic_daily`) reads HAC t ≈ 0 on the null
(`stpat_effect=0`) and crosses HAC t = 2 once a real bump is planted
(`stpat_effect` ≳ 4 vol-units on 99 years). The engine works; the real tape simply
has no detectable effect.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Event mean +14.8 bps but HAC t = 1.13; vs other March days
  Welch p = 0.299. The effect lives entirely in one post-1990 regime and is negative
  before it. No version clears the inference bar.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** One round-trip a year, ~13 bps net (HAC t = 0.98),
  dominated by passive buy-and-hold. No tradable vehicle exists.
- **Busted — a one-regime bump dressed as a holiday rally.** The placebo is flat,
  nothing survives Bonferroni, and the sub-period split exposes the bump as luck
  confined to the last 35 years.
